source.title_on_document: Analogical reasoning with large language models: a co-creative framework and benchmarking of LLMs in design ideation

supplement.where: Included Appendices A-E, PDF pp. 31-34. A separate external supplement is not stated.
supplement.holds: Appendix A: problem statements (p. 31, Table A1); Appendix B: example ideas (p. 32, Figure B1); Appendix C: expert-rater profiles (p. 33, Table C1); Appendix D: participant questionnaire (p. 33); Appendix E: informed consent form (p. 34, Figure E1). No additional outcome standard errors are supplied in these appendices.

paper_design_summary: A pool of 24 first-year undergraduate design students at IIT Hyderabad was selected and randomly paired into teams, then divided between free ideation with internet resources (including Wikipedia and ChatGPT) and ALIA-assisted ideation; the ALIA session lasted 30 minutes, and random condition allocation was not stated (pp. 11, 15-16). Six expert raters scored 36 shortlisted ideas in two sets of 18 (nine ideas per condition in each set) for novelty and quality on 5-point scales; the number of distinct student contributors to these ideas was not reported (pp. 13, 18). A separate model-only Analogical Creativity Task compared three LLMs using 18 sampled analogies, with an unresolved rater-count discrepancy: Methods reports five PhD-scholar raters (p. 14, Section 4.5.2), whereas Limitations reports three raters (p. 26, Section 6.4.2).

studies.label: Idea-generation experiment with ALIA (pairs of design students)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Team condition: ideation with the ALIA LLM support tool versus ideation without a prescribed method (internet, Wikipedia and ChatGPT permitted). Pairing of participants into teams is stated as random. Assignment of teams to the two groups is described only as 'divided', with no statement that it was random.
assignment.quote: All participants were randomly paired to form teams and then divided into either the control or experimental group.

arms.name: ALIA-assisted (experimental)
arms.description: Pairs ideate with ALIA, a desktop LLM tool that transcribes the discussion and supplies trigger questions, analogies and dialectical statements across four timed stages (30 minutes); ideas written on sticky notes. Section 5.2 reports 12 participants in the ALIA group for interaction feedback (p. 18), but the number of people represented in the shortlisted-idea analysis is not stated (p. 13, Section 4.4.4).

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Pairs see the problem statement on a screen and generate concepts without a prescribed method; online resources such as Wikipedia and ChatGPT were permitted (p. 16, Section 4.6.2; Figure 5 on p. 15 labels this arm 'Human (access to internet)'). Actual ChatGPT uptake is not reported. The paper does not explicitly report this arm's randomized or analyzed person count.

participants.exclusions: No participant exclusions are reported. The reported pool is 24 selected students (p. 15, Section 4.6.1). The scored-output analysis uses 36 shortlisted ideas in two sets of 18, with nine ideas from each condition in each set (p. 13, Section 4.4.4); the number of distinct student contributors is not stated. The paper says 'Each of the six teams' after describing random pairing (p. 16, Section 4.6.1); the overall team count is unresolved. The 12 ALIA-group participants reported in the interaction-feedback results (p. 18, Section 5.2) are not confirmed as the people represented among the rated ideas.
participants.who: First-year undergraduate design students (novice designers), working in pairs
participants.quote: A total of 24 first-year undergraduate design students from the Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad, were selected for the idea-generation tasks.
participants.locator: p. 15, Section 4.6.1; ALIA arm size p. 18, Section 5.2 ('Among the 12 participants in the ALIA-assisted group')

ai_tool.name_model: ALIA (Analogical LLM Ideation Agent), built on Mistral 7B (p. 25, Section 6.4.1), with speech-to-text and COSTAR prompt templates
ai_tool.how_used: Runs during a group session, transcribes and summarizes the pair's discussion, and displays LLM-generated How-Might-We questions, analogies, dialectical statements and idea suggestions on screen; also moderates timing of four stages (6, 8, 6, 8 minutes) (pp. 10-12, Sections 4.4.1-4.4.2; p. 16, Section 4.6.2).

task.description: Generate design concepts for problem statements about everyday-life experiences (Appendix A), written on sticky notes

outcomes.name: Expert-rated novelty of ideas
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Six expert raters with industry and/or academic backgrounds, in two sets of three; each set rated 18 shortlisted ideas (nine per condition) on a 5-point Likert scale for 'How unique is the idea compared to existing solutions in this context to you?' (p. 13, Section 4.4.4). That section describes all raters as having more than 10 years in the design industry, but Appendix C, Table C1 (p. 33) lists academia-only experience for some raters and shorter industry tenures for others. Cronbach's alpha was 0.632 for set 1 and 0.715 for set 2 (p. 18, Section 5.1). Mann-Whitney U tests were used, but the analysis unit and analysis n are not explicitly stated; each idea was independently rated by three experts (p. 18, Section 5.1).

contrasts.reported: ALIA-assisted M = 3.31, SD = 1.02, median 3.00, 95% CI [3.04, 3.59]; control M = 2.21, SD = 1.11, median 2.00, 95% CI [2.01, 2.62]; Mann-Whitney U = 770.0, p < 0.05. Figure 6 prints the control mean as 2.31, not 2.21.

outcomes.name: Expert-rated quality of ideas
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same six expert raters and shortlisting design as S1-O1; each idea was independently rated by three experts on a 5-point Likert scale for 'How feasible, practical and useful is the idea within the context?' (p. 13, Section 4.4.4; p. 18, Section 5.1). Mann-Whitney U tests were used, but the analysis unit and analysis n are not explicitly stated.

contrasts.reported: ALIA-assisted M = 3.22, SD = 1.25, median 3.00; control M = 3.17, SD = 1.48, median 3.00; Mann-Whitney U = 1431.0, p > 0.05.

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people assigned. Three LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Mixtral-8x7B) generated analogies under three synectic prompt strategies; 18 analogies (six per model) were sampled for expert evaluation (p. 14, Sections 4.5.1-4.5.2). Methods reports five expert raters (p. 14, Section 4.5.2), whereas Limitations reports three raters for the 18-analogy sample (p. 26, Section 6.4.2). The exact rater count cannot be reconciled from the document.
assignment.quote: In ACT, expert raters evaluated a curated dataset of analogies generated by the researchers.

participants.who: No human ideators. The evaluators are described as PhD scholars with formal academic design training. Methods reports five expert raters (p. 14, Section 4.5.2), but Limitations reports three raters for the 18-analogy sample (p. 26, Section 6.4.2); the discrepancy is unresolved.
participants.quote: Human evaluation was conducted, where five expert raters assessed the analogies based on the creativity criteria of novelty, usefulness and elaboration quality.
participants.locator: p. 14, Section 4.5.2; conflicting rater count on p. 26, Section 6.4.2

ai_tool.how_used: Models generate analogies from source-target concept pairs; no person uses them (p. 14, Section 4.5.1).

task.description: LLM generation of cross-domain analogies for design problems

eligibility.reason: S1 reports a pool of 24 selected students (p. 15, Section 4.6.1). The number represented among the 36 shortlisted ideas is not stated (p. 13, Section 4.4.4), but the entire reported pool is below 50, so criterion 2 is not met. Criterion 1 remains unclear: pairing was random, but random allocation of teams to conditions is not stated (p. 16, Section 4.6.1). Control participants could use internet resources including ChatGPT, with actual ChatGPT uptake unreported (p. 16, Section 4.6.2; p. 33, Appendix D), so the comparison is structured ALIA support versus mixed-resource access. Criterion 3 is met because novelty and quality were scored on participants' ideas (pp. 13, 18). Retain context_class = none because the condition-allocation method is unresolved, rather than confirmed nonrandom. S2 is model-only (pp. 14-15). List S1 in the screening report as a small controlled experiment.

one_line_finding: With 24 design students in pairs, ideas from the ALIA-assisted group received higher expert novelty ratings (M = 3.31 vs 2.21, Mann-Whitney U = 770.0, p < 0.05) and similar quality ratings (3.22 vs 3.17, U = 1431.0, p > 0.05) than the control group (p. 18, Section 5.1).
